1962, Monthly Bulletin of the Ministry of Health and Public Health Laboratory Service, page 188:
A zucchino is a small marrow, but there can be no connection with Shelley’s ‘The Zucca’, which was not drafted until 1821.
A sweet zucchinilike vegetable that can be eaten raw in salads.

e: Borrowed from Italian zucchini, plural of zucchino, diminutive of zucca (“squash”). Ultimately related to courgette through the original Latin cucurbita. Compare Sicilian cucuzza.
Borrowed from Italian zucchetto, ultimately a diminutive of zucca (“gourd, squash”), due to the shape. Compare zucchini.
From Italian zucchina, alternative form of zucchino (plural zucchini).
q: The squashes are used by Italians for frying and other purposes are very small, and for this reason they are called “Zucchine” or small squashes.[…]The “Zucchine” are an extremely tasty vegetable and they are especially good when fried.
